title: Why Your Classroom Routines Must Be Longer
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that combining routines or adding extra steps to them — rather than keeping them minimal — is essential because plain, short routines are inherently boring and boredom is what breeds misbehavior. His central claim is that students need built-in purpose and challenge even in mundane transitions, and that injecting novelty (a quick dance, a vocabulary call-out, an unusual step) turns routine into something engaging rather than deadening. He connects routine quality directly to academic performance, arguing that sloppy, low-standard routines transfer into sloppy, low-standard work, while routines performed to a high bar build a broader culture of excellence. The concrete technique is simply lengthening or merging existing routines with small added challenges, which he says takes almost no planning time. He frames this as a low-effort, high-return adjustment that any teacher can make immediately to counter the boredom-driven behavior problems common in today's classrooms.
points: Add small, engaging twists to normally dull routines — quick dances, poses, or vocabulary call-outs — to keep them from becoming deadening.
Boredom and low standards in routines are described as the "death knell" of a healthy classroom culture.
Treating transitions and routines with the same standard of excellence as academic work is framed as essential, not optional.
Combining or lengthening routines takes little to no extra planning but produces outsized behavioral dividends.
quotes: You can combine two or more classroom routines into one or add steps to an existing routine. Either way, longer routines are better.
Your students need goals to accomplish. They need targets, lined up one after the other, to shoot at.
Boredom, low-bar standards, laziness, and indifference are the death knell of healthy classroom culture.
You must ensure your students maintain a level of focus throughout the entirety of their time with you, whether for one period or the whole day.
Hard work, good performance, and motivation all transfer. And so do their opposites. Therefore, if you accept mindless and sloppy routines, student work will suffer.
The same old, same old just doesn’t work anymore. Times have changed. You must adjust or this job will crush you, as it’s currently doing to so many teachers.
